characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 3 h shows 559.4 ± 5.2 HV, far below the alloy's peak hardness, consistent with only partial α→β-Mn transformation at this condition.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; 5 repeated measurements per sample, average reported
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify the aging hardening response of the 19Al alloy after aging at 550 °C for 3 h

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Bright β-Mn network along α grain boundaries with additional intra-granular short rod-shaped precipitates.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fig. 9 panel for 19Al aged at 550 °C for 3 h (100 µm scale bar)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of secondary α-Mn and β-Mn phases in the aged 19Al alloy

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting of high-purity (>99.9%) raw materials
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 15, 17, 19) ingots produced in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled to plates of 4 mm thickness

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq).
Solution-treated 19Al samples aged at 550 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal state defining the current sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times, average reported

phases_present.morphology: bright network along α grain boundaries plus intra-granular short rod-shaped precipitates

structures.overall_structure: Partially transformed structure: an α (BCC) matrix with a bright β-Mn network along the α grain boundaries plus intra-granular short rod-shaped β-Mn precipitates; the α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy is not yet complete at 550 °C / 3 h.

unmapped_findings: EDS chemical composition of the 19Al alloy (at.%): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0 (Table 1, b0013/table_001).

For the 19Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation was only completed after 10 h of aging at 550 °C, so the 550 °C / 3 h sample remains in a partially transformed state; 17Al required only 6 h at 550 °C (b0053, b0065).

The precipitation kinetics of β-Mn decreased with increasing Al content, attributed to Al enrichment around β-Mn hindering its growth and to the stabilizing effect of Al on the Al-rich D0₃ phase (b0065).
